findings.title: Converting a DOCX with a large table span can exhaust the host process
findings.summary: A small DOCX can place a very large positive value in `w:gridSpan`, `w:gridBefore` or `w:gridAfter`. PDF/PNG/report layout turns that value into vector lengths without a column budget, causing disproportionate allocation or an abort before returning a conversion error.

severity.rationale: Untrusted document producers can deterministically exhaust or abort the embedding renderer. Likelihood is high for a caller that converts attacker-supplied documents; impact is confined to availability of that process, with no established remote deployment.
severity.changeConditions: Dedicated subprocess limits reduce impact; an exposed shared conversion service would increase operational impact.

confidence.rationale: Static trace connects positive usize XML values to two unconditional allocation sites after admission; no semantic span cap exists on this path. No runtime reproduction was executed.

taxonomy.category: Uncontrolled resource allocation from document metadata

codeEvidence.label: Public conversion enters admitted layout
codeEvidence.explanation: `docx_to_pdf`, PNG and reports share `with_layout`; admission limits ZIP/XML structure, then layout parses the body.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded cell span
codeEvidence.explanation: `w:gridSpan/@w:val` is parsed as `usize` with only a lower bound; the untrusted value becomes `RawCell.colspan`.

codeEvidence.label: Unbounded omitted grid columns
codeEvidence.explanation: `gridBefore` and `gridAfter` likewise accept every positive `usize` and become synthetic cell spans.

codeEvidence.label: Span drives column allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: Row occupancy becomes the length of a `Vec<f32>` without a semantic column limit.

codeEvidence.label: Span drives merge allocation
codeEvidence.explanation: The same span later sets the length of a vector of merge records, amplifying memory use.

rootCause.summary: The renderer parses attacker-authored table span attributes into `usize` and preserves them in raw cells, including synthetic cells for omitted columns. `table_block` sums the spans and allocates a column vector of that size; `resolve_table_merges` then allocates merge tracking to the same extent. XML byte, depth and attribute budgets do not restrict these numeric values. For example, a one-cell span of 1000000000 requests roughly 4 GB for columns alone despite requiring only ten digits in XML.

findings.remediation: Apply a documented maximum table grid width to cell and omitted-column spans before raw-cell construction; use checked accumulation and reject over-budget occupancy before allocating or iterating. Enforce the same limit in merge bookkeeping.

counterEvidence: Package admission bounds compressed/inflated bytes, entry counts, XML attributes and depth.
SECURITY.md asks callers to apply CPU/memory process limits; those contain host impact but do not let the API return a bounded refusal.
limitations: No application code or vulnerability input was executed; no deployment exposure is asserted.
validation.summary: Validated public conversion -> admitted layout -> `cell_span`/`row_grid_skip` -> raw cell occupancy -> `Vec` expansion. `stretch_stale_spans` skips rows whose used count exceeds existing columns and does not clamp hostile spans. Admission does not inspect grid span semantics.

dataflow.summary: DOCX XML span -> positive usize -> RawCell.colspan -> occupancy -> column and merge vectors
dataflow.outcome: memory exhaustion, panic or process abort

impact.why: Availability of the CLI or embedding process; no confidentiality/integrity compromise established.

likelihood.why: A short decimal attribute directly controls allocation on an ordinary supported conversion path.

reachability.summary: The public in-process renderer accepts document bytes and uses this table parser after admission, which checks structure rather than numeric table semantics.
reachability.outcome: loss of availability of the rendering process
preconditions: Victim processes the supplied DOCX through layout; attacker needs no host filesystem/configuration access.

attackPath.summary: Supply a valid small DOCX containing a table cell with `w:gridSpan w:val="1000000000"`, then have the victim convert it to PDF/PNG or request page layout. The table model attempts multi-gigabyte allocation.

remediationTests: Convert a minimal admitted DOCX with a huge gridSpan and assert a typed resource refusal before allocating.
Cover huge gridBefore/gridAfter and multiple individually valid spans whose sum exceeds the grid budget.
preventiveControls: Use shared semantic allocation budgets for document-controlled counts in every layout path.

findings.title: Converting Markdown with cyclic drawing dependencies can abort the host
findings.summary: The `drawing:` image envelope accepts dependency indices but materializes them recursively without cycle detection or memoization. A tiny valid envelope in Markdown can make one dependency reference itself, causing unbounded recursion and allocations instead of a conversion error.

severity.rationale: A document producer can reliably terminate or exhaust the in-process converter through ordinary Markdown input. Impact is process availability; no remote service or privilege escalation is assumed.
severity.changeConditions: A shared conversion service increases operational impact; a resource-limited disposable process contains it.

confidence.rationale: Parent source validation confirms an in-range self-reference takes the recursive branch repeatedly; the default public Markdown conversion path reaches materialization. No runtime trigger was executed.

taxonomy.category: Missing cycle control in document dependency graph

codeEvidence.label: Markdown accepts drawing envelopes
codeEvidence.explanation: A Markdown image destination beginning with drawing: is decoded and added as Content::Drawing without graph validation.

codeEvidence.label: Decoder only deserializes JSON
codeEvidence.explanation: Shallow attacker-controlled JSON becomes Drawing/Dep/PayRel objects, including integer dependency indices.

codeEvidence.label: Materializer follows the root index
codeEvidence.explanation: A root relationship part index selects dep_part if within deps length; cycles are not checked.

codeEvidence.label: Dependency traversal has no cycle detection
codeEvidence.explanation: Every dependent relationship recursively calls dep_part, with no active/visited index set, depth limit or memo table.

codeEvidence.label: Capture permits graph cycles
codeEvidence.explanation: DOCX capture memoizes a part before descending, so cycles can be encoded even by the trusted writer; capture limits do not protect materialization.

rootCause.summary: `picture` recognizes a caller-authored `drawing:` destination and `decode` base64-decodes it into serde graph structs. Package assembly invokes `materialize`, which follows a root `part` index into `deps`. `dep_part` reserves a fresh name and clones XML, then follows every dependent `part` index by calling itself before writing or memoizing the current part. A root pointing to dependency 0 whose own relationship points to 0 repeats indefinitely. Capture's 64-part limits are not validated by decode and would not rule out a one-node cycle anyway.

findings.remediation: Validate drawing dependency graphs on decode and materialization. Use a visited-index map with reserved output names before recursion, reject unsupported cycles, and enforce depth, dependency count and cumulative byte budgets independently of capture.

counterEvidence: DOCX capture limits parts, relationships and bytes and memoizes captured parts; the materializer neither reuses that memo nor validates graph cycles.
Caller process resource limits constrain availability impact but cannot turn stack overflow into a recoverable conversion error.
limitations: Static validation only; no malicious input or application code was executed.
validation.summary: Confirmed markdown_to_docx -> read/picture -> package::assemble/drawing -> materialize -> dep_part. Bounds checks prove indices exist but do not establish acyclicity. `used` is a name-collision set rather than a graph-visit set. serde recursion limits concern nested JSON, not integer graph cycles.

dataflow.summary: Markdown drawing: URI -> base64/serde graph -> Content::Drawing -> package materialize -> repeated dep_part(0)
dataflow.sink: recursive dependency traversal with per-call allocation
dataflow.outcome: stack overflow/process abort or memory exhaustion

impact.why: Terminates or exhausts the current process.

likelihood.why: A small shallow JSON envelope can express the required integer cycle.

reachability.summary: Public markdown::markdown_to_docx accepts the Markdown directly; CLI and bindings wrap this library boundary. No image-loader callback or filesystem authority is needed.
preconditions: A victim converts the supplied Markdown.

attackPath.summary: Have the victim convert Markdown containing a `drawing:` JSON envelope with a root dependency 0 and a dependency relationship back to 0. Default conversion reaches recursive materialization and cannot return normally.

remediationTests: Convert an inline drawing envelope with a self-cycle and assert a bounded typed refusal.
Cover a two-node cycle, deep acyclic chain, repeated shared dependency and over-budget graph.
preventiveControls: Treat integer-indexed serialized graphs as untrusted graphs rather than assuming capture-produced invariants.

originalCandidate.originalEvidence: Confirmed static DoS candidate: src/markdown/from_docx/drawing.rs dep_part at 1956-2007 recursively follows attacker JSON rel.part at 1973-1974 without visited/memo/depth guard; decode at 1397-1408 only base64+serde. A single drawing dep whose rel.part=0 loops forever, creating new names and cloning XML until stack/OOM. Reachability: Markdown write::picture 4189-4197 accepts payload; package::drawing 1703-1712 invokes materialize->dep_part (1893-1894). Capture side memoizes at 608-610, so cyclic DOCX part relationships are also preserved into payload.

candidate.originalEvidence: read() calls main_text before other validation (legacy_doc.rs:180-193). main_text verifies contiguous logical CP ranges (1157-1175), but each Piece may reuse same physical fc and pushes a StoryChar per CP (1181-1221), with ccp_text directly read u32 (919), no output budget. A ~1 MiB WordDocument stream and ~4096 PCDs each referencing the same 1 MiB physical text can demand ~4 billion StoryChars from ~1.1 MiB input. Finite file-sector bounds do not limit this logical expansion.

deferred.reason: Focused investigator reports admission/DOM grammar differential; awaiting parent validation.

candidate.originalEvidence: main XML `<w:document xmlns:w='…' a=x b="x><n><n>...(100000 times)..."> </w:document>`. Admission TagPolicy::tolerant accepts unquoted a=x and sees all `<n>` inside quoted b, depth=1. DOM Parser::parse_element instead treats unquoted x as the opening quote, consumes through next x at b's start, then takes b's embedded `>` as root delimiter and recursively parses the hidden `<n>` sequence without depth checks. WmlDocument::from_bytes admission -> lazy main_document reaches it; inspect strict validation counterguards this malformed fixture.
